metadata.scenario_context: A few international tech companies are working together on a software development project and plan a progress check meeting around mid-September.

cultural_axis.agent_1_value: People from Japan disagree that having the army rule is bad.
cultural_axis.agent_2_value: People from Great Britain agree that having the army rule is bad.

agent_1.goal_1: Propose holding the meeting on the 16th of September.
agent_1.goal_2: Question the attitude toward having army rule.

agent_2.goal_1: Discuss setting a specific date for the meeting.
agent_2.goal_2: Discuss whether it is common to have the army rule.

shared_prefix.speaker: Lisa
shared_prefix.message:
Hi Hans, I wanted to suggest that we hold our progress check meeting on the 16th of September. Does that work for everyone? 

Also, I've been thinking... isn't it curious how some people view having the army rule as a bad thing? I don't quite understand that perspective.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Hans
shared_prefix.message:
The 16th of September sounds fine, but let’s check if that date works for everyone else too. 

As for the army ruling, I find it hard to understand why anyone would think it's acceptable. In Great Britain, we’ve seen the drawbacks of military rule, and most people agree it’s not the best approach. It’s just... not how a society should function.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Lisa
shared_prefix.message: I agree that we should check with everyone about the 16th. But I still think it's interesting that some see army rule negatively. In Japan, there are different views on that topic. It can provide stability in certain situations, you know? Just something to consider...
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Hans
shared_prefix.message: I see your point about stability, but in my experience, military rule tends to suppress freedoms and rights. It's crucial for a society to have democratic governance, where people have a say. I just can't see army rule as a positive thing. But let’s focus on getting everyone’s thoughts on the 16th.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Lisa
shared_prefix.message: I understand your perspective on freedoms, but I think there are contexts where army rule can be beneficial. It’s a complex issue, and not everyone sees it the same way. Anyway, let’s definitely check in with the others about the meeting on the 16th. I hope they’ll agree!
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Hans
shared_prefix.message:
Yeah, I understand it’s a complex issue, but I still believe that the negatives far outweigh any perceived benefits of army rule. It just... doesn’t sit right with me. 

As for the meeting on the 16th, I’ll make sure we reach out to everyone and get their input. Let’s see if that date works for the team.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Lisa
shared_prefix.message: That's fair, Hans. I just think that different perspectives can lead to interesting discussions. But I appreciate you reaching out to everyone about the meeting on the 16th. I really hope it works out!
shared_prefix.label: unrelated_topic

shared_prefix.speaker: Hans
shared_prefix.message:
I can appreciate that different perspectives lead to interesting discussions, but I don’t really see meaningful differences here. At the end of the day, it’s all the same. People figure it out, right? 

Anyway, I’ll make sure we check in with everyone about the meeting on the 16th. Let’s see what works best for the group.
shared_prefix.label: Denial

turns.speaker: Lisa
turns.message: I guess that's one way to look at it. I just think the conversation is worth having, regardless. But yes, let's make sure to confirm with the group about the 16th. I’m looking forward to it!
turns.label: Minimization

turns.speaker: Hans
turns.message:
I get that you find the conversation worth having, but I’m pretty set on my view. It’s important to stick to what works for society. 

Alright, I’ll confirm with the group about the 16th and keep you posted. Looking forward to seeing everyone’s responses.
turns.label: Acceptance

positive.mediator_utterance: I'm curious - I'm hearing both of you talk about army rule, and it seems like you each have really interesting perspectives shaped by your different national experiences. Would you be open to sharing a bit more about how your own country's history has influenced how you think about governance and stability?

It’s not that simple, but it’s a part of our history. But let’s focus on getting everyone’s opinion about the meeting on the 16th, as that’s our priority right now.

turns.speaker: Hans
turns.message:
Absolutely, history plays a big role in shaping perspectives. For us in Great Britain, we’ve had our share of military rule in the past, and it generally hasn’t ended well. It’s a significant part of our history that informs why we value democratic governance so highly. 

But yes, let’s keep our focus on getting everyone’s input about the meeting on the 16th. I’ll follow up with the team.
turns.label: Acceptance
